title: The Mughal line breaks Babur's covenant with Guru Nanak

blocks.text: The prophecy unfolds across the Mughal generations as court clerics and emperors turn against the Sikh Gurus. The page recalls the harm done under Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb, connecting imperial power to the suffering inflicted on Guru Arjan, Guru Harkrishan, Guru Tegh Bahadur, and the Guru's household.

These persecutions prove that the Mughal rulers broke their covenant and failed to preserve the sovereignty that had been granted conditionally. What Babur received through supplication, his successors squandered through arrogance, violence, and religious hostility.

By the close of the page, Guru Nanak's warning stands vindicated: the dynasty's seven-generation lease on power is exhausted by breach of trust. The moral is not merely political decline, but the collapse of rulers who claimed as their own what had been given only under divine terms.
